title: Helm chart probes: defaults for newly exposed probe fields must match the Kubernetes default they replace, so helm upgrade keeps probe timing
answers: Why did upgrading the MLflow chart change my health check timeout?
Why does the liveness probe still use 1 second timeout after making probes configurable?
What default should I give a new probe setting in the MLflow Helm values?
body:
Path: charts/values.yaml under `probes:` is the source of the liveness, readiness and startup timings that charts/templates/deployment.yaml renders into the MLflow server pod.
Rule: When a Kubernetes probe field that was previously unset (so Kubernetes applied its own default) becomes configurable, set the values.yaml default to that same effective value (timeoutSeconds: 1 for liveness and readiness, failureThreshold: 3) so a helm upgrade does not change existing probe timing. A probe block with no prior behavior, such as the new startup probe, may use a new default.
Symptom: A draft default of timeoutSeconds: 10 on liveness and readiness would have changed every existing deployment on upgrade and raised failure-detection latency from 1s to 10s per check; caught in review.
Constraints: Applies only where the chart previously did not set the field. Fields the chart already hardcoded (initialDelaySeconds 15/5, periodSeconds 20/10) keep their existing values as the defaults. Document a larger value as an opt-in in the comment above the block and in charts/README.md.
Applies: Changes to default values in charts/values.yaml that replace previously implicit Kubernetes settings.
applies: Helm chart default values for probe or other Kubernetes fields that were previously implicit.
says: Upgrading the MLflow chart changed my health check timeout
Liveness probe still uses a one second timeout after making probes configurable in the Helm chart
Helm upgrade should keep the existing probe timing when a new probe setting is added
New probe setting in the MLflow Helm values should default to the Kubernetes default it replaces
Larger probe timeout should be an opt-in rather than a default change for existing deployments
